prompt: Use case: style-transfer and design revision. Create a THIRD candidate for 'All Accounts Due' that balances two failed directions. Image 1 is the original cover: preserve its meaningful six-chamber bronze accounting device, central pointer, dark mood and title. Image 2 is too intricately rendered for an expressive oil painting: DO NOT repeat its miniature spokes, hardware, and granular texture. Image 3 is too simple: DO NOT use flat pie-chart sectors. Make a rich but selective Group of Seven inspired oil-painted novel cover with a single imposing round bronze mechanism. Show SIX distinct broad inset chambers, each with a different recognizable large painted material or symbol (green stone fragments, copper discs, pale folded papers, dark coal, ochre shards, and warm golden fragments); render each with a few grouped strokes, not individual tiny pieces. Keep a clear central bronze pointer and a handful of strong structural seams, enough to read as a crafted device. Surround it with spacious, atmospheric midnight blue and burnished gold brush masses, and reserve crisp detail for chamber silhouettes, pointer, and title. Avoid uniform impasto on every part, microscopic cracks, needles, gears, labels, and intricate filigree. Exact integrated title 'All Accounts Due' once, fully legible at top. 9:16 portrait book cover, no new people, text, border, author name or watermark.
qa_concern: User approved this as detail benchmark; study candidate only.

prompt: Use case: style-transfer with substantial visual simplification. Asset type: revised candidate novel cover. Image 1 supplies the title and essential symbols only: a dark sun with light emerging, seven choices below, and open receiving hands. Image 2 is a painting-style reference only; do not copy its heart, figure, city, or objects. Recompose as an expressive Group of Seven inspired oil painting made of broad, calm color masses. The sun is ONE strong dark disk with a simple bold golden split; seven wide golden paths or color bands descend toward SEVEN plain arched openings. The arches are simple silhouettes with no inner stairs, room detail, decoration, or fine linework. Near the bottom, a pair of open hands are suggested with broad brush planes and readable silhouette rather than individually detailed fingers or skin texture. Use warm gold against deep charcoal and indigo, dramatic light, atmospheric negative space, and visible large brushwork. No tiny cracks, spidery threads, narrow rays, small objects, or uniform impasto on every surface. Let the painting breathe and read at thumbnail size. Render the exact title 'Daughter of the Sun' once, accurately and legibly at the top, integrated into the art. 9:16 portrait book cover. No other text, figures, author name, border or watermark.
qa_concern: Simplifies seven openings and light; compare with source for symbolic fidelity.

prompt: Use case: illustrated-story novel cover, fresh composition inspired by an existing cover. Image 1 is a CONTENT reference for this story, not a pixel template. Image 2 is only the approved balance of selective detail against broad oil-painted masses; do not copy its wheel, colors, or title. Paint a fresh 9:16 novel cover called 'The Apes Above'. The visual idea from Image 1 must stay recognizable: a bright circular sky opening above an ancient stone arena with a tiny distant craft and trail; at a dark stone desk, three intelligent dinosaur characters—an armored broad-faced dinosaur in center, a blue-and-rust feathered dinosaur at left, and a horned dinosaur at right—look upward or toward each other; a crowd is present behind them. Simplify the composition enough for confident oil painting: the three foreground heads and gestures are the only detailed focal forms; central armor is FIVE OR SIX large interlocking plates with just a few bold spikes, not hundreds of scales; feathered companion reads from a few long color sweeps; horned companion from a strong silhouette. Audience is a rhythmic mass of dark silhouettes, not individually rendered creatures. Arena wall is large warm and cool planes, no tile grid. Keep the tablet as a simple dark rectangle on the desk; no extra small object is necessary. Visible varied brushwork with rich atmospheric light, but no repeated tiny mosaic chips or scale-by-scale texture. Preserve expressive faces and anatomy; painted, not cartoon. Render exact title 'The Apes Above' once, legibly within the bright sky opening. No other text, border, author name or watermark.
qa_concern: Fresh composition improved crowd/architecture; central armor still has fairly fine scales.

prompt: Revise Image 1, the existing painted-v1 candidate of 'What the Town Owed Her', into a stronger, simpler oil painting. Image 1 is the edit target; Image 2 is the original cover, used only to check story content and composition. Image 3 is a style reference for bold painted masses, not a source of subjects or scenery. Keep the 9:16 portrait layout, the exact title 'What the Town Owed Her' once at the top in readable ivory serif letters, and the same two women: the back-facing dark-haired visitor at left and the dark-haired woman in a long black dress in the warm right doorway. Retain the visitor's paper and keys, the cold rainy window on the left, and candle warmth on the right. Preserve their poses, relative size, and emotional tension. The v1 has too much individual detail. Simplify the note to one pale paper plane with only faint marks, keys to one compact glinting cluster, and window panes/rain to broad cool blue strokes. Reduce the hanging herbs, candles, wood trim, curls, buckles, and dress buttons into a few suggestive shapes. The viewer should first see a broad blue rain mass facing a broad amber doorway mass, then the two women. Use varied, sweeping, painterly brush strokes and thick color planes with selective sharp accents only at faces, hands, paper, keys, and title. Avoid covering every small component with separate impasto marks. Avoid excessive outlines, tiled texture, stippling, CGI smoothness, or new props. Keep the original mood and story identity.
qa_concern: Selected study candidate after visual comparison; fine paper and keys remain as meaningful focal props.
